name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.119.0 — Retained review and replay evidence artifacts are written as single-line .jsonl under .claude/spec-runs/ instead of pretty-printed .json. A pretty-printed artifact in a tracked host path is reformatted by any host gateCommand that formats .claude/ — the first non-empty evidence array reddened the close gate on a file the session never wrote (salon-os, 2026-09-09), and a formatter running --write over retained evidence would rewrite the bytes /spec:escape's killedMatch derives from. .jsonl is the shape no source formatter claims a parser for; artifacts retained earlier keep the .json extension and stay readable, since promotion walks the directory and /spec:escape reads by path. The close-time gate refusal now tells the reader to check which path the gate output names before editing anything, since the pipeline's own artifacts under .claude/ are in the host's rule surface but are never files to hand-edit. 7.118.0 — Citation checker resolves prose-lookback citations instead of skipping them. A citation whose preceding words name no file ("authored against § Design Canon") is now checked against the citing file plus every file in spec/doctrine, derived from the directory so a new doctrine file joins with no edit. The resolution is deliberately weak: a heading matching nothing in that union stays SKIP and can never become a MISS, because ordinary English before a section mark cannot be told apart from a real file reference and a strong resolution there would turn correct doctrine red. Repo-wide coverage goes from CHECKED=88 SKIP=104 to CHECKED=158 SKIP=34, MISS still 0; the remainder are host-generated pipeline-rules sections the checker skips by design. 7.117.0 — Driver-stepped command files (build, review, run, mocks) stop restating what their drivers print at runtime — every envelope, exit, cap and remedy now arrives from the driver at the step where it is needed, once. Every command's Rules section is capped at 8 bullets and every shared-for section list is pinned exactly, so a section cannot join a command's read surface silently. The host pipeline-rules file is documented as path-scoped and arrives with the config Read, so no command re-reads it, and the genesis discovery brief is edited in place per answer and rendered in full only once, at discovery's end.
